framework.name: Department of Basic Education · Basic Education Competency Framework
framework.approvalContext: DBE describes the framework as approved in 2024 for the national Curriculum Strengthening initiative.
framework.sourceBoundary: This crosswalk references the DBE framework. It does not represent DBE approval, accreditation or certification of Applied Commerce or BIS.

knowledge.definition: What learners learn and understand, including declarative, conceptual and procedural knowledge within disciplines.

skills.definition: How learners apply what they know.

characterAndAttitudes.definition: How learners think, feel and behave.

values.definition: What learners consider important; values sit at the centre of the framework.
values.note: The source page refers back to the 2001 Manifesto on Values, Education and Democracy. This file does not infer a complete values taxonomy beyond the items explicitly named in the retrieved framework material.

allowed: Evidence in this programme is mapped to the DBE Basic Education Competency Framework area: <area>.
The learner demonstrated programme evidence relevant to <area> in the defined task/context.
The programme creates opportunities to practise and evidence <area>.
prohibited: BIS has officially assessed or certified DBE competency attainment.
A mapped response proves permanent mastery of a DBE competency.

mappings.rationale: Self-knowledge and revisable self-understanding support reflection on thinking/learning and openness to development.
Agency and initiative require purposeful self-direction, responsiveness and willingness to act/learn.
Evidence evaluation, claim limits, observation and interpretation are direct critical-thinking and metacognitive practices.
Behaviour change requires self-management, recovery, revision and reflection on one's own process.
Planning and prioritisation require deliberate goal management, monitoring and trade-off reasoning.
Decision and judgement require evaluating evidence, alternatives, consequences and responsibility.
Value creation and enterprise combine problem solving, idea generation, communication and sustainable economic participation.
Financial capability uses quantitative reasoning, evidence and resource stewardship.
Systems thinking analyses relationships, feedback, leverage and wider consequences.
Risk, resilience and protection require recovery, responsive planning, judgement and responsibility.
Communication, influence and negotiation require clear expression, listening, interaction and judgement.
Leadership and ethical responsibility are evidenced through work with others, communication and responsibility for consequences.
Career and life navigation require adjustment, development, professional communication and sustainable pathways.
Long-horizon leverage and legacy reasoning require systems judgement, responsible design and future-oriented economic thinking.
Transfer and meta-learning explicitly require reflection on learning, adaptation to new contexts and reasoned revision.

aggregationRule: Sponsor/cohort reports may aggregate evidence against DBE-mapped areas only after the underlying BIS competency evidence is reportable, privacy thresholds are satisfied and the language remains 'mapped/relevant to' rather than 'certified attainment'.
